caption:
A stunning poem by @arielj.music about the upper limits in all of us. 🖤

Our brains just want to keep us safe & sometimes that means keeping us in our comfort zones. I hope this can inspire you to do some mindset work today to show your subconscious that it’s all okay, and the view up that high is worth it xx

Listen to my podcast, COZY with Alyssa Daphne, for more mindset mastery and positive vibes. 🖤
author: Alyssa Daphne | Self Growth & Cozy Mindset Mastery
transcript: I started getting what I asked for and I got scared. I almost handed it back because I ain't never been up that high. I started living how I asked for and then I rebelled like I was under attack because I ain't never been up that high. I started flying like I seen it in my dreams for years and then I fell, scared of wings blowing out my back because I ain't never been up that high. But when I hit the ground, see the soil held me close and whisper, you'll do well. Hug the air and she will hug you back. I know you never been up that high. Then the rain came to wash me clean. A strike of lightning set some fire to my dreams and the wind climbed up under my wings, lifting me up again with one big swing and I was flying. Beaming with pride, I know the elements of cracking a smile. I think I'm ready now. Wow, I ain't never been up this high.
title: The Upper Limit: Fear of Your Own Success
one_liner: A spoken-word poem captures how we self-sabotage when life finally gives us what we wanted.
key_points: We instinctively resist or retreat when we start achieving our goals — because it's unfamiliar territory
The brain treats success like a threat, triggering self-sabotage to return to the comfort zone
Hitting rock bottom can be a reset — a moment of grounding before trying again
Mindset work is needed to convince the subconscious that thriving at a higher level is safe
